title: Power of randomization in scheduling with obligatory tests
formal: Determine R_rand=inf_A sup_I E[cost_A(I)]/OPT(I) for obligatory-test scheduling with t_j=1 and an oblivious adversary.
definitions: There are n≥1 labeled jobs available at time zero on one unit-speed machine. Job j requires a test of known duration t_j>0 followed, at some possibly later time, by processing of duration p_j≥0. Only completion of its test reveals p_j. Both operations are nonpreemptive, occupy the same machine and cannot overlap any other operation. Other jobs may be tested or processed between the two operations of j. The scheduler initially knows n and all t_j, but has no upper bounds or prior distributions for p_j. All durations are real, operations of zero processing duration complete immediately when scheduled, and arbitrary history-dependent policies are allowed with no computational restriction. C_j is the completion time of the processing operation and cost is ∑_j C_j. OPT knows all p_j in advance but must execute every test and obey the same single-machine and precedence constraints. No additive competitive term is allowed. Here every t_j is exactly 1. Policies may use private random bits; expectations are over those bits. An oblivious adversary fixes n and the entire processing-time vector before the random bits are drawn, although the policy sees each p_j only after its test. The optimal ratio is the infimum over randomized policies, with one policy covering all n. A policy must finish every job almost surely and its expected cost must be finite on every instance.
answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute distance from the defined optimal ratio is at most 1/100. Certified upper and lower bounds with gap at most 1/50 qualify via their midpoint. Bounds must cover all instances and all competing policies as quantified; attaining the infimum or supremum is not required.
context: The source distinguishes unit tests from arbitrary test times and leaves randomized performance as a further question.
why: This isolates the value of randomization in scheduling with compulsory information acquisition.

import_provenance.original_title: The power of randomization in scheduling with obligatory tests
import_provenance.original_statement: Determine the optimal randomized competitive ratio against an oblivious adversary for single-machine total completion time when every initially available job must undergo a unit-time test revealing its unknown processing time. Both test and processing operations are nonpreemptive, and the offline optimum must also test every job.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: This is the randomized direction explicitly proposed in the paper; the deterministic uniform-test bounds are √2 and 1.585. The 2026 result on gradually arriving jobs concerns flow time and does not resolve this all-jobs-present model: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12716

sentences: All jobs are available initially and each requires a unit-duration test.
Testing reveals the processing time without executing the processing itself.
A randomized scheduler is compared with an offline schedule obeying the same tests.
The instance is fixed before the scheduler draws its private random bits.
The target is a worst-instance ratio of expected total completion time.
